chunks.title: ARTICLE I. RECOGNITION
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer hereby recognizes the Union as the exclusive bargaining agent for full time covered employees at the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility, and Riverside Correctional Facility Philadelphia, PA with respect to wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment described in this Agreement.

Section 2. All full time employees in the following classifications are covered under this agreement:
(1) Data Entry Clerk
(2) Secretary
(3) Supply Clerk
(4) Carpenter/Locksmith
(5) Electrician
(6) Electronic Locksmith
(7) Maintenance Mechanic
(8) Stationary Engineer
(9) Maintenance Trades Helper
(10) Laborer
(11) Building Engineer
(12) Supervisor Mechanic, Kitchen Equipment
(13) Maintenance Mechanic, Kitchen Equipment
(14) Maintenance Trades Laborer, Kitchen Equipment
(15) Painter
(16) Plumber

* Maintenance Trades Helper shall principally be aligned with a particular trade category (electrical, plumbing, maintenance mechanic).

Section 3. The Maintenance Trades Helper shall bid into a skill trade category with no change in pay.

Section 4. It is understood that a Maintenance Trade Helper will work primarily in the particular trade category with which he or she is aligned. However, Maintenance Trades Helpers may be assigned to assist other trades as needed.

chunks.title: ARTICLE II. UNION SECURITY
chunks.text:
Section 1. It shall be a condition of employment that all full time employees of the Employer covered by this Agreement who are members of the Union in good standing on the effective date of this Agreement shall remain members in good standing and those presently employed who are not members on the effective date of this Agreement or the signing date of this Agreement, whichever shall be later, shall become a member in good standing. It shall also be a condition of employment that all full time employees covered by this Agreement hired on or after the effective date shall, on or before the thirtieth (30th) calendar day following the beginning of such employment, become and remain members in good standing in the Union.

Section 2. When new or additional employees are needed, other than in an emergency situation, the Employer shall notify the Union as to the number of employees needed. The Union shall have 48 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays) in which to fill the Employer's request for new or additional qualified employees, thereafter, the Employer shall be free to fill his needs from other sources.

chunks.title: ARTICLE II. UNION SECURITY
chunks.text:
Section 3. The Employer shall be the sole judge of the qualifications for all applicants and reserves the right to reject any applicant referred by the Union for employment. In addition, it is a condition of the Employer's contract with the City of Philadelphia that the contracting agency may reject an applicant or require removal of an employee who:
(1) Receives an unsuitable report after the agency processes the employee's background investigation, or if the agency finds the applicant/employee to be unsuitable or unfit for his/her assigned duties, and/or;
(2) Who violates prison rules and regulations.

Section 4. The Union shall notify the Employer in writing of the names of all shop stewards.

chunks.title: ARTICLE III. NON-DISCRIMINATION
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer and the Union both recognize their responsibilities under Federal, State, and Local law pertaining to fair employment practices as well as the moral principles involved in the area of Civil Rights. Accordingly, both parties affirm by this Agreement a commitment not to discriminate against any person or persons because of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, sexual preference, disability, medical condition, age, or status as a disabled veteran of wars including Vietnam, as long as the individual is qualified to perform the duties of the job.

Section 2. Where the designations man, he, his, etc. appear, it is accepted and understood by the parties to this Agreement that these terms shall apply equally to males and females.

chunks.title: ARTICLE IV. GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION PROCEDURE
chunks.citation: CBA Article IV — Grievance and Arbitration Procedure
chunks.text:
Section 1. Should differences arise between Employer and the Union as to the application or interpretation of the provisions of this Agreement, the Union shall have the right to settle these differences by filing a grievance in the following manner. The employee shall be entitled to union representation at every step of this process.

Step 1. The aggrieved employee shall, within seven (7) calendar days of the occurrence of the events giving rise to the grievance, discuss the matter with the applicable supervisor and attempt to resolve the grievance.

Step 2. If the grievance is not satisfactorily adjusted in Step 1, it shall be reduced to writing no later than seven (7) calendar days from the answer in Step 1 on forms mutually agreed upon, signed by the aggrieved employee and a Union Steward and stating the date the grievance arose, a statement of the grievance, and the remedy requested. The written grievance shall be submitted to the employer's Assistant Project Manager, who will meet with the employee and a Shop Steward to discuss the matter. A written answer to the grievance shall be given within seven (7) calendar days of the meeting with the Assistant Project Manager.

chunks.title: ARTICLE IV. GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION PROCEDURE
chunks.citation: CBA Article IV — Grievance and Arbitration Procedure
chunks.text:
Step 3. If the grievance is not satisfactorily adjusted in Step 2, the decision may be appealed by written notice to the Director of Human Resources or her/his designee with the same powers, within seven (7) calendar days of the Step 2 answer. The Business Manager or his designated representative and the Shop Steward shall meet with the Director of Human Resources, within fourteen (14) calendar days in an attempt to resolve the matter. The Director of Human Resources shall give a written answer within seven (7) calendar days of the meeting in Step 3.

Step 4. If the decision in Step 3 is not acceptable to the Union, the Union must notify the Employer within thirty (30) calendar days of the receipt of the Step 3 answer of its intention to submit the grievance to arbitration.

(1) The parties shall utilize the services and procedures of the American Arbitration Association under its voluntary arbitration rules and regulations. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding upon the parties, the arbitrator shall have the authority to interpret and apply the provisions of the Agreement, but shall have no power to add to, detract from, or alter its terms.

(2) Each party shall pay its own costs in arbitration, except that the non-prevailing party shall be responsible for payment of the Arbitrator's entire fee.

chunks.title: ARTICLE IV. GRIEVANCE AND ARBITRATION PROCEDURE
chunks.citation: CBA Article IV — Grievance and Arbitration Procedure
chunks.text: Section 2. It is the intent of the parties that any grievance be submitted promptly and processed with reasonable promptness. Therefore, grievances which are not submitted and processed within the time limits set forth above shall not be considered or processed further except by mutual consent of the parties. If a decision is not rendered within the times established, the grievance shall be deemed to be denied and the grievance may be appealed to the next step.

chunks.title: ARTICLE V. SENIORITY RIGHTS
chunks.text:
Section 1. Seniority with the Employer shall determine seniority for the purpose of bumping, layoff, and recall; for all other purposes, including promotion, transfer, shift preference, and overtime assignments, seniority within the trade classification shall be used to establish seniority. All service time in a trade classification will be considered worked in, and only in, the craft to which the employee is primarily assigned. In the event of a tie, the employee with the highest last three digits of Social Security Number shall be deemed to have the highest seniority within the group of tied employees.

Section 2. When subject to layoff, employees may bump into lower paid classifications, assuming they possess the necessary qualifications and are senior to the employee they are bumping.

Section 3. Recalls shall be based on the inverse order of layoffs, i.e., last person laid off is first person recalled. These recall rights will be for a period of two (2) years. As an exception, Shop Stewards, as long as they hold office, shall be the last to be laid off, and the first to be recalled, regardless of the length of their trade classification seniority.

Section 4. Classification seniority shall govern in establishing preference for vacations.

chunks.title: ARTICLE V. SENIORITY RIGHTS
chunks.text: Section 5. Seniority shall be lost by an employee if the employee is on a verified and approved continuous illness or disability leave or for all verified and approved work-related injuries or illnesses that are for a period of time in excess of six (6) months. Notwithstanding the foregoing, it is understood between the parties that the Employer may discontinue benefits regarding the above after an employee is absent for twelve (12) weeks of verified and approved leave.

chunks.title: ARTICLE VI. DUES DEDUCTIONS
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer agrees to deduct the Union Dues and assessments, if any, from the pay of those employees who individually request in writing that such deductions be made. Except as otherwise provided under the Union security provisions of this Agreement, the authorization shall be irrevocable during the course of this Agreement. The amounts to be deducted shall be certified to the Employer by the Union and the aggregate deductions of all employees shall be remitted together with an itemized statement to the Union by the last day of the succeeding month after such deductions are made.

Section 2. The Union shall indemnify and hold the Employer harmless against any and all claims, orders, or judgments brought or issued against the Employer as a result of any action taken or not taken by the Employer under the provisions of the Article.

Section 3. The company agrees to pay the union a monthly assessment of $120.00 for part time on call employees. The assessment fee is based on a fixed number of 24 part time on call employees who are cleared and have received the required orientation by the correctional facility, and a flat rate of $5.00 per part time on call employee.

chunks.title: ARTICLE VI. DUES DEDUCTIONS
chunks.text: Section 4. The Employer agrees to deduct and transmit to the IUOE, Local 835 Political Action Fund, contributions from the wage of those employees who voluntarily authorize such deduction in writing in accordance with applicable law as soon as the Employer receives notice from the Union that this Fund has been established. The Union shall furnish the Employer the necessary authorization forms. The Employer agrees to transmit the amounts deducted by the last day of the succeeding month after such deductions are made.

chunks.title: ARTICLE VII. PROBATIONARY EMPLOYEE
chunks.text:
Section 1. An employee shall be considered a probationary employee until he has worked for and completed ninety (90) calendar days following the beginning of such employment with the Employer. The probationary period may be extended up to an additional sixty (60) calendar days at the discretion of the Employer, upon notification to the Union. A probationary employee shall have no seniority rights and the Employer may discipline and/or terminate such employees as it finds necessary, and they shall have no recourse to the grievance procedure. After completion of the probationary period, seniority shall begin on the day of hire.

Section 2. An employee who is promoted, demoted, or transferred to a new classification shall be considered a probationary employee within that new classification for thirty (30) calendar days after the effective date of the personnel action. Union rights shall remain intact during this probationary period. During that period, the employee has the right to return to his/her former classification, or the employer may return that employee to his/her former classification.

chunks.title: ARTICLE VIII. UNION BUSINESS REPRESENTATION
chunks.citation: CBA Article VIII — Union Business Representation
chunks.text: Section 1. Authorized representatives of the Union shall have access to the work site where employees covered by this Agreement are employed, at any time. They must notify the Employer prior to any visit for the purpose of investigating and adjusting employee complaints, and providing they do not interfere with the work of the employees. The Union recognizes that prior approval of the customer is required before obtaining access to the premises, and that the customer may deny access to the prison.

chunks.title: ARTICLE IX. STEWARDS/NEGOTIATIONS
chunks.text:
Section 1. Stewards, Officers, and Negotiating Committee members shall not be penalized for required attendance at grievance or negotiating sessions. They shall be paid for such time at their normal rates of pay, plus shift differential, if applicable, for normally assigned shifts, provided, however, that the number of paid Union representatives at negotiating sessions shall not exceed four (4).

Section 2. Shop Stewards shall conduct Union business on their scheduled breaks and lunch, except for meetings with management relating to the discipline of bargaining unit employees, or meetings called by the Company, which shall occur whenever necessary.

Section 3. A shop steward who wishes to discuss Union business with a supervisor shall request a meeting, which shall be scheduled as convenient to both parties.

chunks.title: ARTICLE X. OCCUPATIONAL INJURIES
chunks.text:
Section 1. An employee involved in an accident or receiving an injury on the job must report such incident to the Supervisor as soon as possible, and must complete the appropriate forms.

Section 2. An employee injured on the job will be paid for work time lost while being medically treated for such injury on the day of injury and subsequently up to a maximum of five (5) days for time lost due to medical treatment and not covered by Workers' Compensation. The employee must sign the form which permits the Employer to recover any Workers' Compensation payable to the employee for the first five days' lost time. No employee will be taxed twice on payment for the same period.

Section 3. The employer agrees to provide and maintain all required safety equipment.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 1. Employees who are covered by this Agreement shall earn paid time off in two categories, at the annual rates indicated below:

Scheduled Time Off:
Years of Service | Scheduled Time-Off Days
1 year but less than 5 years | 15
5 years but less than 10 years | 20
10 years but less than 20 years | 25
20 years or more | 30

Unscheduled Time Off:
Each employee will be entitled to nine (9) days of unscheduled paid time off per year.

New hires shall receive (subject to accrual) eight (8) STO days and five (5) UTO days during the first year of employment. After attaining one year of service, the employee will receive the number of STO and UTO days provided above.

Section 2. Paid time off in each category is accrued per pay period. Unscheduled Time Off becomes available for use at the end of the employee's probationary period. Scheduled Time Off becomes available for use at the end of six (6) months of employment. Paid time off may not be advanced for use, and no employee may use any more time than he or she has accrued as of the date of proposed usage.

Section 3. Paid time off in each category must be used in whole (eight-hour) days, except that sixteen (16) hours of Unscheduled Time Off may be used in two-hour increments.

Section 4. All paid time off will be paid at the employee's regular hourly rate.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 5. To request approval for Scheduled Time Off, the employee must complete and submit a Request for Leave form no later than ninety-six (96) hours prior to the requested start date of the Scheduled Time Off. Approval for valid requests will not be unreasonably withheld, and the employer shall use its best efforts to promptly notify the employee whether the STO has been approved or denied. Requests not submitted within the required notification limit may be disapproved. An employee will provide the Employer with one (1) day's notice (24 hours) of his/her intention to cancel Scheduled Time Off.

Section 6. To request approval for Unscheduled Time Off, the employee must notify the Supervisor or Assistant Project Manager no later than one (1) hour prior to the start of the employee's shift.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 7. In the case of an unscheduled absence covering more than one day, the employee must notify the Supervisor or Assistant Project Manager no later than one (1) hour prior to the start of the employee's shift, and must indicate his/her expected date of return to work. The employee may elect to use either Scheduled Time Off (the 4-day notice requirement being waived by the Company) or Unscheduled Time Off for the second and subsequent day only (2 days in total of STO) of a continuous absence (so long as the employee has both UTO and STO time in his/ her bank), two (2) times per year, provided that should an employee be absent for four (4) consecutive days or longer, he/she must present a Doctor's note upon return to work in order to avoid an attendance violation. If an employee has exhausted UTO, the employee may use STO without restriction, but is subject to an attendance violation.

Section 8. Authorized paid holidays occurring during periods of vacation are counted as holidays, not as Scheduled or Unscheduled Time Off.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 9. Paid time off which has accrued but has not been used may be carried over on the employee's anniversary date. The amount to be carried over shall not exceed ten (10) days of Scheduled Time Off and seven (7) days of Unscheduled Time Off. Paid time off in either category which exceeds the carry-over limit will be forfeited on each employment anniversary.

Section 10. Employees who, as of (date of contract with City) have an accrued balance of either Scheduled or Unscheduled Time Off in excess of the carryover limit, may, at that time only, transfer an amount of time from one category to another sufficient to avoid forfeiture of time in either category.

Section 11. Employees may, at their own discretion, use Unscheduled Time Off for a planned absence, provided that they have given the required four (4) day's notice.

Section 12. On April 1 of each year, the Company will post a Scheduled Time Off sign-up schedule for the period May 1 through September 30. Prior to May 1, seniority within each labor classification will govern choice of Scheduled Time Off periods. After May 1, choice of Scheduled Time Off periods will be by date of request. In all cases, a request for one week or more will take precedence. A similar posting and schedule will be established on September 1 for the period October 1 through March 31 of each year.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 13. Employees are entitled to redeem up to one-half (1/2) of their available paid time off balance for cash, at their regular rate of pay. This cash redemption may be implemented by an employee no more than one time in any twelve-month period. Payment of the cash redemption will take place as part of regular payroll processing.

Section 14. Employees who voluntarily terminate employment after providing the required two week advance notice will be paid for available, unused Scheduled Time Off, and unused Unscheduled Time Off, accrued to the date of separation, provided that they work the two week notice period. Employees who are terminated by layoff will be paid for available, unused Scheduled Time Off and unused Unscheduled Time Off, accrued to the date of separation. Employees who are discharged for cause, or who fail to give or work the required two (2) weeks notice or fail to return company or customer property, will not be paid for any paid time off.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
Section 15. Emergency Unscheduled Time Off ("EUTO")
The provisions of Sections 5 and 6 of this Article do not cover a situation in which an employee who is already at work needs emergency time off from that shift, due to personal illness or to household emergencies, etc. In these cases, the employee is unable to give management the required notice. Therefore, the following procedures are being established to provide uniform handling of such situations.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
(1) While at work, the employee shall notify his or her supervisor in writing (Leave Request Form) as soon as the situation becomes known, and shall tell the supervisor how much time he or she is requesting off on that shift.
(2) The employee will be required to provide documentation of the nature of the emergency. The required documentation will be reviewed by management to determine whether the emergency time off will be treated as authorized or not authorized. All Emergency UTO time will be submitted as unpaid leave until the documentation is approved by management.
(3) Authorized Emergency UTO will not be subject to disciplinary action, and will be changed from unpaid to paid time, providing that the employee has sufficient accrued UTO time at the beginning of the pay period to cover this absence and any prior absence during the pay period.
(4) If documentation is not presented by the employee as soon as is practicable, but not to exceed within 7 (seven) calendar days of the employee's return to work, the Emergency UTO will be characterized as unauthorized and unpaid, and will be subject to discipline as a Time/Attendance violation.
(5) If, in the opinion of management, documentation presented is not sufficient to establish authorization, the Emergency UTO will be characterized as unauthorized and unpaid, and will be subject to discipline as a Time/Attendance violation.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
The Employer will not unreasonably withhold authorization.
(6) If the absence is characterized as unauthorized and unpaid, the employee will not be paid for the Emergency UTO, even if he or she has accrued UTO time available.
(7) If the absence is characterized as unauthorized and unpaid, and occurs on the employee's scheduled shift immediately prior to a holiday, the employee will not be paid holiday pay for that holiday.
(8) Presentation by the employee of false documentation in any situation covered by this policy will be cause for disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
(9) Emergency UTO may not extend beyond the single shift in which it occurs. If the employee requires additional time off in connection with the same incident, the existing contractual provisions for request and usage of time off apply.
(10) Employees who have been notified, under the provisions of the Substance Abuse Policy, that they are required to take a substance abuse test, may not use Emergency UTO for that time period.
(11) Emergency UTO, if authorized, may be used for the amount of time required, and is not required to be used in two-hour increments.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XI. TIME BANK
chunks.text:
This provision shall not be construed to modify Article XI, Section 3 of the CBA, providing that sixteen (16) hours of Unscheduled Time Off may be used in two-hour increments.
(12) Emergency UTO shall be capped at six (6) instances per calendar year.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XII. NO STRIKE/NO LOCKOUT
chunks.citation: CBA Article XII — No Strike/no Lockout
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Union agrees that during the term of this Agreement it will not cause, sanction, or permit, nor will any member of the Union cause or take part in any strike, work slowdown, or stoppage, sit-down, walkout, picket, sympathy strike, or any curtailment of work, or any restriction of services or interference with services in any of the Company's premises.

Section 2. The Company agrees that during the term of this Agreement, it will not lockout the employees covered by this Agreement.

Section 3. Both parties agree to comply with this Article during the term of the Agreement or until arbitration has been exhausted and the party against whom the decision has been rendered refuses or fails to abide or comply with such decision.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XIII. SUBCONTRACTING
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer will endeavor to do all its maintenance work covered by Employer's contract with the City of Philadelphia with its own forces. No maintenance work shall be performed by outside contractors in lieu of working overtime by its own work force. However, this would not apply when there are restrictive time limits on a job which is not within the limits of the work force or in cases where special skills, tools, or equipment may be required, or where the City of Philadelphia specifically requires the use of a subcontractor.

Section 2. The Employer will give the Union notice at a reasonable time prior to the subcontracting of any maintenance work which would have a direct impact on the employees covered by this Agreement. Also, when equipment is purchased installed, the seller may install the equipment to protect guarantee rights, and in addition to do such work as may be covered by the warranty.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XIV. MANAGEMENT RIGHTS
chunks.text: Section 1. Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, nothing herein shall limit the Company in the exercise of the rights and functions of ownership or management.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XV. PAID LEAVES OF ABSENCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XV — Paid Leaves of Absence
chunks.text:
Section 1. All Requests for Leaves of Absence as authorized below shall be made in writing on a Request for Leave Form and submitted to the appropriate Assistant Project Manager for approval. Such approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

Section 2. Employees in an approved leave of absence shall accumulate seniority during such absence.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XV. PAID LEAVES OF ABSENCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XV — Paid Leaves of Absence
chunks.text:
Section 3. Military Leave:
(a) Employees who have short term (i.e., no longer than 14 calendar days) military reserve or national guard training/service may be granted up to ten working days military leave. Upon return to work, the employee will be paid the difference between his or her military pay and the regular rate of pay, plus shift differential, if applicable, for their position, up to eight (8) hours per day, for up to ten (10) work days. Employees who must serve in excess of ten (10) work days will be granted unpaid leave for the military service period exceeding ten (10) days.
(b) The employees regular rate of pay will be at the regular hourly rate, plus shift differential, if applicable, up to eight (8) hours per day.
(c) The employee will be paid only for those days which he would normally have been scheduled to work, up to ten (10) work days.
(d) Military duty pay will be computed based on the regular rate of military pay, exclusive of all allowances for rations, subsistence, and travel.
(e) In order to receive payment under this Section, an employee must give the Company prior notice to such military duty and, upon his return to work, must furnish the Company with a statement of his military duty pay while on such duty.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XV. PAID LEAVES OF ABSENCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XV — Paid Leaves of Absence
chunks.text:
Section 4. Funeral Leave:
(a) In the event of the death of an immediate family member, employees are authorized paid leave to attend the funeral. Employees are authorized up to four (4) working days to attend a funeral within a 400 mile radius; or up to five (5) working days for a funeral over 400 miles away.
(b) Immediate family member is defined as the employee's spouse, parents, brother, sister, children, or legal guardian.
(c) In the event of the death of other family members, employees are authorized paid leave to attend the funeral, as follows:
Parents-in-Law, Grandparents - Three (3) days
Brother-in-Law, Sister-in-Law - One (1) day
(d) Employees should notify their Assistant Project Manager of a Request for Funeral Leave as soon as possible under the circumstances.
(e) The employee's rate of pay will be at the regular hourly rate, plus shift differential, if applicable, up to eight (8) hours per day.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XV. PAID LEAVES OF ABSENCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XV — Paid Leaves of Absence
chunks.text:
Section 5. Jury Duty:
(a) Employees who are required to serve on Jury Duty may be granted up to ten (10) working days paid leave. The employee will be paid the difference between the jury pay and expenses they receive and their regular rate of pay, plus shift differential, if applicable. Periods of Jury Duty in excess of ten (10) working days will be granted as unpaid leave.
(b) The employees regular rate of pay will be at the regular hourly rate, plus shift differential, if applicable, up to eight (8) hours per day.
(c) The employee will be paid only for those days which normally would have been scheduled for work.
(d) In order to receive approval under this Section, the employee is required to present a notice issued by the Clerk of Court calling him/her to jury duty to their Assistant Project Manager as soon as possible after receipt, but no later than ten (10) working days prior to service.
(e) In order to receive payment under this Section, the employee is required to present notice from the Clerk of Court stating the number of days served and the compensation received.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XVI. SHIFT DIFFERENTIAL
chunks.text: Shift differential is included in the employee's hourly rate. Employees whose shift starts after 12:00 p.m., (e.g., 12:01 p.m. or later) will receive the shift differential of $1.50 per hour for that shift.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XVII. HOURS OF WORK
chunks.citation: CBA Article XVII — Hours of Work
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer shall be free to fix the hours of employment provided that a normal work week for each employee shall consist of forty (40) hours. The work week commences at 0001 hours, Monday, and ends at 2400 hours the following Sunday.

Section 2. For the purpose of computing overtime hours, all Scheduled Time Off and Unscheduled Time Off, exclusive of Scheduled Time Off and Unscheduled Time Off cashed in, and paid holidays, shall be included in hours worked. Time and one-half shall be paid for all hours worked in excess of eight hours per day on weekday shifts and in excess of 12 hours per day on regularly scheduled 12-hour weekend shifts. In addition, time and one-half shall be paid for hours worked in excess of 40 in the workweek. Employees whose shifts start after 12:00 p.m., (e.g., 12:01 p.m. or later) will receive the shift differential of $1.50 per hour for that shift.

Section 3. The Employer will endeavor to arrange regular shifts and work schedules and will not make indiscriminate changes of such schedules. A shift shall be considered as worked on the calendar day on which it begins.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XVII. HOURS OF WORK
chunks.citation: CBA Article XVII — Hours of Work
chunks.text:
Section 4. Kitchen Equipment workers will work an eight (8) hour day between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and 8:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. Individual work schedules will be established by the Project Manager, and will be based on the kitchen equipment work requirements. Kitchen Equipment workers will receive the applicable shift differential whenever they are required to work outside of their normally assigned hours.

Section 5. There will be a paid thirty (30) minute lunch period. Employees must not leave the site (or go building to building) during the lunch period. Employees may leave the building after notifying supervision as to general location of where they will be. However, a supervisor may require that the employee remain in the building for extenuating circumstances or safety reasons which shall not be unreasonable.

Section 6. Personnel Files: Verbal warnings, written warnings, and suspensions will not be considered in progressive discipline after 12 months from the date of the last incident upon which they were based.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XVII. HOURS OF WORK
chunks.citation: CBA Article XVII — Hours of Work
chunks.text:
Section 7. Payroll discrepancies will be promptly investigated by Headquarters, upon notice from the employee through her or his supervisor. The employee shall provide information about the specifics of the discrepancy. If the discrepancy is found to be the fault of the company, a supplementary check will be mailed within 3 work days of receipt by Headquarters of the complaint.

Section 8. The following number of employees may be permitted off simultaneously on any non-holiday:

Three (3) bargaining unit employees from CFCF on the 8:00 am to 4:00 pm shift
Two (2) bargaining unit employees from CFCF on the 4:00 pm to 12:00 am shift
One (1) bargaining unit employee from CFCF on the 12:00 am to 8:00 am shift

Two (2) bargaining unit employees from RCF on the 8:00 am to 4:00 pm shift
Two (2) bargaining unit employees from RCF on the 4:00 pm to 12:00 am shift
One (1) bargaining unit employee from RCF on the 12:00 am to 8:00 am shift

chunks.title: ARTICLE XVIII. CALL-IN PAY
chunks.text:
Section 1. An employee recalled to work after completion of his/her regular shift, or called back to work on his/her regularly scheduled day off shall be guaranteed a minimum of four (4) hours pay at the appropriate pay rate.

Section 2. The employee shall receive the appropriate overtime rate for all hours worked.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XIX. HOLIDAYS
chunks.text:
Section 1. Employees shall receive eight (8) holidays with pay on the following days: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth Fourth of July, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.

Section 2. All covered full time employees are eligible for the designated holidays if they are working or on an approved absence (i.e., scheduled time off “STO” approved at least four (4) days in advance) on the scheduled work day prior to and the scheduled work day after a designated holiday. For the Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. shift only, if a holiday set forth in Section 1 of this Article falls on a Saturday, it shall be celebrated on the preceding Friday. If such a holiday falls on a Sunday, it shall be celebrated on the following Monday. If an employee calls out on a holiday they are scheduled to work, then they must provide a physician’s note (within seven (7) days) in order to receive holiday pay.

Section 3. Holiday pay will consist of the employee’s regular hourly rate, plus shift differential, if applicable, for eight (8) hours. On all designated holidays that an employee is required to work, he/she shall receive one and one-half (1 ½) times their regular rate of pay plus holiday pay. Employees must actually work the holiday to receive holiday pay of 1 ½ times their regular rate of pay.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XIX. HOLIDAYS
chunks.text:
Section 4. The following number of “essential employees” may be permitted off simultaneously on a holiday:

Two (2) bargaining unit employees from CFCF on the 8:00 am to 4:00 pm shift
Two (2) bargaining unit employees from CFCF on the 4:00 pm to 12:00 am shift
One (1) bargaining unit employee from CFCF on the 12:00 am to 8:00 am shift

Two (2) bargaining unit employees from RCF on the 8:00 am to 4:00 pm shift
Two (2) bargaining unit employees from RCF on the 4:00 pm to 12:00 am shift
One (1) bargaining unit employee from RCF on the 12:00 am to 8:00 am shift

Essential employees are those working as an Electrician, Stationary Engineer, Maintenance Trades Helper, Building Engineer, and Plumber. Employees in classifications other than those listed above are not required to work their regular scheduled shift if it falls on a holiday or when a holiday is scheduled. In addition, one (1) locksmith shall be considered to be an “essential employee” on the CFCF 8:00 am to 4:00 pm shift.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XX. PENSION
chunks.text:
Section 1. Employer shall pay monthly into the Central Pension Fund of the International Union of Operating Engineers and Participating Employers for each eligible employee at the amount specified in Section 3 below.

Section 2. Payments to the Pension Fund required above shall be made to the Central Pension Fund of the International Union of Operating Engineers and Participating Employers which was established under an Agreement and Declaration of Trust dated September 7, 1969. The Employer agrees to be bound by all of the terms and conditions of that Agreement and Declaration of Trust and by any amendments to said Trust Agreement.

Section 3. It is agreed that the Employer’s contribution to the Pension Fund shall be:

1. Effective July 1, 2022 - $1.80 per hour worked (capped at 40 hours)
2. Effective July 1, 2023 - $2.00 per hour worked (capped at 40 hours)
3. Effective July 1, 2024 - $2.20 per hour worked (capped at 40 hours)
4. Effective July 1, 2025 - $2.40 per hour worked (capped at 40 hours)

It is agreed that all Employer contributions shall be made within thirty (30) days after the date required by the Trustees. Contributions will be made to the address supplied by the Pension Fund, as that may change from time to time.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XX. PENSION
chunks.text: Section 4. All covered full-time employees are eligible to participate in the 401(k) plan established by the Company for the benefit of its employees. Union members shall participate under the same terms and conditions as all other participants. The Company shall transmit 401(k) deferrals on a bi-weekly basis.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXI. WAGES
chunks.text:
Section 1. The wage rates and classifications that apply are shown in Exhibit “B”.

1. Effective July 1, 2022 — 4% increase to base wages
2. Effective July 1, 2023 — 3.75% increase to base wages
3. Effective July 1, 2024 — 3.75% increase to base wages
4. Effective July 1, 2025 — 3.5% increase to base wages

Exhibit “B” shall be modified to reflect the agreed upon wage increase. Exhibit “B” shall also be corrected to reflect the $1.50 shift differential as set forth in Article XVII (“Hours Worked”), Section 2.

Section 2. All wages are to be paid biweekly. When employees are terminated, they shall be paid all wages or other compensation due not later than the next regular payday on which wages would otherwise be due and payable as prescribed by Pennsylvania Wage Payment and collection law.

Exhibit “B” — WAGE RATES

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXII. HEALTH CARE INSURANCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XXII — Health Care Insurance
chunks.text:
Section 1. The Employer will provide Group Long Term Disability (LTD) coverage for all full time eligible employees.

(a) Group LTD coverages, benefits, claims procedures and eligibility requirements are as described in the U.S. Facilities Plan Document, which is made a part of this agreement by reference.

(b) The Employer reserves the right to change insurance carriers, modify, alter, or improve the Group LTD Plan, but will maintain equivalent coverage for participating employees.

Section 2. The Employer agrees to make contributions to the Local 835 Health and Welfare Fund to provide the following benefits for all covered employees and their dependents: Medical, Prescription Drug, Vision, Life Insurance, Accident and Sickness Insurance. Contributions shall be as set forth in Exhibit “A”.

Section 3. The Employer agrees to provide dental coverage for all bargaining unit employees pursuant to the benefit structure set forth in its current U.S. Facilities’ Dental Plan. Employees shall not be responsible for any contributions toward dental premium payments during the term of this Agreement.

Exhibit “A” — HEALTH AND WELFARE CONTRIBUTIONS

The amounts below represent the total amount to be contributed per hour worked, up to a maximum of forty (40) hours per week to the Health and Welfare Fund.

Through June 30, 2022 — $11.93 per hour

Effective July 1, 2023 — $12.21 per hour

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXII. HEALTH CARE INSURANCE
chunks.citation: CBA Article XXII — Health Care Insurance
chunks.text:
The Employer’s contribution shall not increase more than 4% per annum in each successive year of the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

For the duration of this Agreement, $0.63 per hour will be deducted from employees’ hourly wages to assist with the Employer’s health and welfare contributions.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Section 1. Safety Committee: A safety committee will be established between the Union and the Employer as follows:

(a) Membership for the Union shall consist of the Shop Stewards; for the Employer, the Assistant Project Managers.

(b) The Safety Committee will meet at least quarterly to consider safety awareness, education, and training; identification of any unsafe conditions.

(c) Any committee member can propose a special meeting, subject to the approval of the Project Manager.

Section 2. Uniforms: The Employer agrees to furnish employees work uniforms, consisting of a hat, five (5) pairs of pants, and five (5) shirts (long sleeve, short sleeve, or a combination), per year, to be worn during working hours while on duty. All uniforms will be distributed between June 1st and August 31st of a calendar year. Employer will Supply one (1) jacket, and one (1) winter hat per year. Replacements for jackets will be made based on fair wear and tear. The employer will pay $100 to each covered employee, if required by his/her position, each year, as a shoe allowance to be paid between August 1st and August 31st of each calendar year.

Section 3. Job Posting: The Employer agrees to post all job openings pertaining to transfer or promotion within the bargaining unit for a period of seven (7) calendar days. Each such posting shall specify the shift for the particular job opening.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Section 4. Bargaining Unit Work: Neither the Project Manager nor the Assistant Project Managers will perform bargaining unit work except if bargaining unit members cannot be obtained to assist in diagnosing a problem or for the purpose of instruction and training.

Section 5. Substance Abuse Policy: This Agreement incorporates the Substance Abuse Policy appearing as Exhibit C.

Section 6. All discipline shall be imposed on an employee within ten (10) days from the date the Employer first became aware of the incident leading to the discipline, unless the Union agrees to an extension of time, or unless the discipline is the result of action by the City. Requests by the Employer for additional time will not be unreasonably rejected. The employer represents that it will not initiate contact with the Prison with the sole purpose of seeking to have an employee barred from the prison.

Section 7. Perfect Attendance Plan

a. Perfect attendance is defined as having no time and attendance violations.

b. An employee who attains a 12-month period of perfect attendance will receive 8 hours pay at the end of that 12 month period. Thereafter, a new 12-month period will start for that employee. Payment shall be made within sixty (60) days of a perfect 12 month period, following notification to the employer by the union.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
c. The 12-month period is a rolling 12 months. That is, if an employee incurs an attendance violation, that employee’s 12 month period begins the day after the most recent violation.

Section 8. (Work Rules). The parties agree to meet and discuss the issue of work and safety rules after ratification.

Section 9. (Random Drug Testing Plan): See attached Exhibit C.

EXHIBIT C. - SUBSTANCE ABUSE POLICY

U.S. Facilities, Inc. is committed to providing a safe and healthful working environment for its employees. Substance abuse threatens the safety and healthiness of the workplace, and threatens our productivity in providing full service to our client by increasing tardiness, illness, and job-related accidents. It reduces judgment, and threatens employee morale. Some of the substances which cause such problems include: alcoholic beverages, controlled drugs (such as tranquilizers, barbiturates and stimulants), and illegal drugs (such as heroin, cocaine, and marijuana).

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
As set forth more fully below, U.S. Facilities is a drug-free workplace that strictly prohibits the manufacture, use, and distribution of controlled substances (as defined below), as well as the consumption of alcoholic beverages in the workplace. Employees who are found to have violated this policy will be subject to discipline, up to and including termination of employment. In addition, treatment, rehabilitation, and/or disciplinary action may be required where an employee’s job performance is affected by off-the-job drug or alcohol abuse, because the abuse of such substances may jeopardize the safety of other employees, employees of our client, the public, and U.S. Facilities or Philadelphia Prison System property.

For these reasons, and in compliance with the federal “Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1989”, U.S. Facilities, Inc., has established the following Substance Abuse Policy for its employees at the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility or at other portions of the Philadelphia Prison System.

DEFINITIONS

For the purposes of this policy, the following terms are defined as noted below:

Alcohol: Any beverage containing alcohol which is capable of producing a physical, mental, emotional or behavioral change in the user.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Company Premise: Includes the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility and/or other facilities within the Philadelphia Prison System that are owned, leased or operated by USF or its clients.

Drug Paraphernalia: Any equipment, device, apparatus which was used by an employee for the purpose of consumption, ingestion or inhalation of illegal drugs.

Illegal Drugs: Includes: (1) any chemical substance whose manufacture, use, possession or sale is prohibited by state or federal law; (2) any legally-dispensable controlled substance (medications available only as prescribed by a licensed physician) obtained fraudulently or used by any individual other than the person for whom prescribed; (3) any over-the-counter medication or substance capable of impairing one’s alertness and/or physical or mental reflexes taken for purposes of abuse or misuse.

Work Day: Work Day includes, in addition to actual working time, break and meal periods, if the employee returns to work after such break or meal period, regardless of whether the individual is on U.S. Facility premises during such time and regardless of whether the individual is paid for such time.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Prescription or Over the Counter Medication: Medication normally taken for medicinal or other legitimate reasons, consistent with directions of a physician or, in the case of over the counter medications, consistent with the directions on the package.

GENERAL POLICY

U.S. Facilities, Inc. prohibits the manufacture, possession, sale, use, being under the influence, distributing or dispensing of illegal drugs and controlled substances, including the possession and or distribution of Drug Paraphernalia, by employees during the Work Day, while on the job, or while on USF or client property (including owned or leased parking facilities), or any other work site.

U.S. Facilities, Inc., also prohibits the manufacture, unauthorized possession, sale, being under the influence, distributing or dispensing of alcohol by employees while on the job, or while on USF or client property (including owned or leased parking facilities), or any other work site. All employees are prohibited from consuming alcohol during any portion of their work day. This shall not prohibit employees from having unopened containers of alcohol in their private vehicles.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
To determine whether alcohol or illegal drugs or controlled substances are located on or are being used on U.S. Facilities, Inc., or Philadelphia Prison System property (including owned or leased parking facilities), or any other work site, USF reserves the right to conduct searches, or to have searches conducted on its behalf, when reasonable suspicion is present.

Any employee whom U.S. Facilities, Inc., has reason to believe is engaged in the manufacture, sale, distribution or possession of illegal drugs or controlled substances or engaged in the manufacture, sale, distribution or unauthorized possession of (excluding unopened containers of alcohol in an employee’s private vehicle) alcohol on U.S. Facilities, Inc., or Philadelphia Prison System property (including owned or leased parking facilities), or any other work site will be subject to discipline up to and including discharge. Employees who are convicted of the manufacture, sale, or distribution of illegal drugs or controlled substances, shall be subject to discipline up to and including discharge. If such conviction occurs by reason of off duty conduct, discipline up to and including discharge will be incurred if the nature of the conduct may be related to, or have an impact upon, the employee’s job.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Employees are required to be fit-for-duty during the Work Day and while on USF premises. An employee is unfit-for-duty if he or she tests positive for drugs or alcohol. A positive drug test includes positive-dilute (defined as a urine specimen with creatinine and specific gravity values that are lower than expected for human urine)..

All records concerning test results will be kept in the employee’s medical files for two (2) years, which are maintained separately from the employee’s personnel file. These files will be considered confidential except that information disclosed in such tests will be communicated to such USF personnel or within the laboratory that need to know such information in order to make appropriate employment decisions about the individual.

TESTING

Random Drug Testing Policy

As set forth in Article XXIII, Section 9 of this Agreement, U.S. Facilities will conduct random drug screenings of its employees, including full-time, part-time and hourly employees, as well as supervisors and managers. USF follows the following guidelines when conducting random drug testing of its employees:

a. All testing will be conducted by a licensed independent medical laboratory, which will follow testing standards established by applicable state and/or federal laws.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
b. Testing will be conducted by urine sample provided by the employee to the independent medical laboratory under procedures established by the laboratory.

c. USF will not participate in selecting person(s) to be tested.

d. USF will not know the test schedule.

e. Tests will be performed during shift. If test runs beyond the end of the employee’s shift, the employee will be paid overtime. All sections of the current plan remain in full force and effect, including provisions relating to rehabilitation for a positive drug test, which shall continue to apply.

f. Refusal to be tested will result in dismissal.

g. All site employees (managers, supervisors, hourly employees, part-time employees, etc.) are included in each pool of persons to be tested.

h. Unless otherwise specified, Tests will be conducted quarterly. Number of persons to be tested quarterly will be no more than 10.

i. Random Drug Testing will be for drugs listed in the policy only and not for alcohol.

j. USF will pay for the cost of the testing. The lab will retain samples in accordance with state or federal law, so that the employee may requests a retest of a the sample at his expense.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
The testing for drugs will be administered by a means selected by the certified independent medical facility. At the time the specimens are tested, two samples shall be taken and a third if requested by the employee. Two samples will be sent to the laboratory to be tested at the employer’s expense. In order to be considered positive, the sample must show positive results on the Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (“GC/MS”) confirmatory test.

The third sample or specimen shall be collected in a separate container and shall be sealed in the presence of a medical facility witness with evidence tape, which tape shall be signed by the witness. This third sample will be sent by the laboratory to another NIDA certified laboratory selected by the employee for testing. The cost of testing the third sample shall be borne by the employee.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text: The employee shall have seventy-two (72) hours to present to USF any different results from the test of the third sample conducted by a laboratory selected by the employee. Neither the employee nor USF is permitted to take physical possession of the third sample. The failure of the employee to have the third test performed or to present the results shall not be used against the employee as a basis for discipline or in any arbitration or other legal proceeding. If the employee chooses not to have the third sample tested, then he/she cannot challenge the accuracy of the results. If the results of the testing of the third sample are negative, the employer will reimburse the employee for the cost incurred by the employee in having the third test performed.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
Unless otherwise directed by the independent medical laboratory, if an employee has a confirmed positive test result, the employee will be contacted by the laboratory to discuss those results and, if the lab technician determines that there may be a legitimate medical explanation for the positive test results, the employee will be given an opportunity to provide a valid prescription for medication that he/she is taking that may have influenced the results of the employee’s drug screening. If the employee provides a legitimate medical explanation for the positive test result that is acceptable to the laboratory, then lab test result will be reported as negative to USF. If the employee fails to provide a valid medical prescription within the timeframe and guidelines allotted by the laboratory, than the test will be reported as positive to USF and the employee will be subject to disciplinary action as appropriate.

REASONABLE SUSPICION

In addition, when U.S. Facilities, Inc. has reasonable suspicion that an employee has used or is under the influence of alcohol, or illegal drugs or other controlled substances while on the premises or any other work site, USF reserves the right to require the employee to submit to appropriate testing procedures, as set forth below.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
The term “reasonable suspicion” shall, as used in this policy, mean generally that there is the existence of a reasonable and articulable belief that the employee is using a prohibited drug or alcohol on the basis of specific, contemporaneous, physical, behavioral, or performance indicators of probable drug or alcohol use. Circumstances or conditions which may support such a belief include, but are not limited to: impairment or deterioration of job performance; exhibition of abnormal mental or physical conditions or behavior; observations relating to speech, appearance, and/or body odor; engaging in or exhibiting conduct which jeopardizes the safety of the workplace, employees, property, or other persons; regulatory or Company rule violations. If the employee is a member of the bargaining unit, a bargaining unit representative shall be notified when an employee is to be tested for reasonable suspicion.

Reasonable suspicion where certain behavior is observed, including but not limited to:

(1) Aberrant or unusual on-duty behavior of an individual employee which:

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
(a) Is observed on duty by the employee’s immediate supervisor or another employee or employee of the client and, in the latter case, confirmed by the observation of another managerial employee; or is observed by other employees or persons, but cannot be immediately confirmed by another managerial employee. In this case, the Director of Human Resources or her/his designated, qualified representative

[Page 24 ends mid-provision; continuation appears on page 25.]

shall investigate the reports. The investigation will include an interview with the employee and witnesses and all observations will be documented, in writing, by the observers; and

(b) Is not reasonably explained by the employee as resulting from causes other than the use of controlled substances or alcohol.

(2) A non-minor on-the-job industrial or traffic accident. In this case, USF may require testing if there is reasonable basis for the belief that employee negligence contributed to the accident.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
(3) Observation by the employee’s immediate supervisor or another USF employee or employee of the client of the use of alcohol, illegal drugs or other controlled substances while on the premises or on any other work site or verifiable information from a USF employee or employee of the client that an individual has used or possesses alcohol, illegal drugs, or other controlled substances while on the premises or any other work site. The Director of Human Resources or his/her designated, qualified representative shall investigate this information and interview the employee in question and witnesses, and all information will be documented in writing.

(4) Return from a leave of absence in excess of ninety days, if the purpose of the leave of absence was related to any form of substance abuse.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text: (5) For purposes of searches, observation by a supervisor, another USF employee, or an employee of the client that the employee is in possession of alcohol (except unopened containers in the employee’s private vehicle), illegal drugs or other controlled substances while on the premises or any other work site, or verifiable information from another USF employee or an employee of the client of such possession. The Director of Human Resources or his/her designated, qualified representative shall investigate this information and interview the employee in question and witnesses and all information will be documented in writing.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text: An employee who reports to work and is considered to be under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs, or controlled substances, will be removed from service immediately. The decision to do this may be made by the employee’s supervisor, the Assistant Project Manager or Project Manager, or the Director of Human Resources or his/her designated, qualified representative. Such a decision will be based on whether the employee is able to perform assigned duties correctly or whether the company’s operation, activities and/or property are adversely affected by the person’s use of such substances. In addition, if USF reasonably suspects that any employee has used such substances on the premises or on any other work site, the individual will be removed from service immediately. U.S. Facilities, Inc. will then follow the procedures set forth below for investigation and/or testing. Refusal to submit to appropriate testing procedures or refusal to permit the disclosure of the results of the testing to the Director of Human Resources or his/her designated, qualified representative is cause for discipline up to and including discharge.

chunks.title: ARTICLE XXIII. MISCELLANEOUS
chunks.text:
When it has been determined that an employee has used or is under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs or controlled substances on the premises or at any other work site, U.S. Facilities may, as a condition of continued employment, require the employee to seek treatment for substance abuse from a recognized treatment center. The employee will then be placed on a leave of absence, and his/her compensation, if any, will be based on the usage of available accrued paid time off, or, in the case of members of the bargaining unit, upon the terms of the Union’s disability coverage. If the employee violates this substance abuse policy, but refuses to initiate or to participate successfully in a treatment program, the employee will be subject to discipline up to and including discharge. After the treatment program has concluded, the employee will be subject to periodic testing, without the requirement of reasonable suspicion being necessary, for a period of one year. If the employee refuses to submit to the testing procedure, or refuses to permit the disclosure of the results of the testing to the Director of Human Resources or his/her designated, qualified representative, the employee will be subject to discipline up to and including discharge.

If a second offense occurs within two years of the first offense, the employee will be discharged.

An employee who has participated in a substance abuse rehabilitation program will not be excused from complying with the rules and regulations of U.S. Facilities, Inc., and the Philadelphia Prison System which are applicable to all other employees.

EXHIBIT C. - SUBSTANCE ABUSE POLICY

U.S. Facilities, Inc. is committed to providing a safe and healthful working environment for its employees. Substance abuse threatens the safety and healthiness of the workplace, and threatens our productivity in providing full service to our client by increasing tardiness, illness, and job-related accidents. It reduces judgment, and threatens employee morale. Some of the substances which cause such problems include: alcoholic beverages, controlled drugs (such as tranquilizers, barbiturates and stimulants), and illegal drugs (such as heroin, cocaine, and marijuana).

chunks.title: Page 21 — Exhibit C — Substance Abuse Policy (definitions)
chunks.text:
As set forth more fully below, U.S. Facilities is a drug-free workplace that strictly prohibits the manufacture, use, and distribution of controlled substances (as defined below), as well as the consumption of alcoholic beverages in the workplace. Employees who are found to have violated this policy will be subject to discipline, up to and including termination of employment. In addition, treatment, rehabilitation, and/or disciplinary action may be required where an employee’s job performance is affected by off-the-job drug or alcohol abuse, because the abuse of such substances may jeopardize the safety of other employees, employees of our client, the public, and U.S. Facilities or Philadelphia Prison System property.

For these reasons, and in compliance with the federal “Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1989”, U.S. Facilities, Inc., has established the following Substance Abuse Policy for its employees at the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility or at other portions of the Philadelphia Prison System.

DEFINITIONS

For the purposes of this policy, the following terms are defined as noted below:

Alcohol: Any beverage containing alcohol which is capable of producing a physical, mental, emotional or behavioral change in the user.

Random Drug Testing Policy

As set forth in Article XXIII, Section 9 of this Agreement, U.S. Facilities will conduct random drug screenings of its employees, including full-time, part-time and hourly employees, as well as supervisors and managers. USF follows the following guidelines when conducting random drug testing of its employees:

a. All testing will be conducted by a licensed independent medical laboratory, which will follow testing standards established by applicable state and/or federal laws.

b. Testing will be conducted by urine sample provided by the employee to the independent medical laboratory under procedures established by the laboratory.

c. USF will not participate in selecting person(s) to be tested.

d. USF will not know the test schedule.

e. Tests will be performed during shift. If test runs beyond the end of the employee’s shift, the employee will be paid overtime. All sections of the current plan remain in full force and effect, including provisions relating to rehabilitation for a positive drug test, which shall continue to apply.

f. Refusal to be tested will result in dismissal.

chunks.title: Page 23 — Exhibit C — Random Drug Testing Policy

g. All site employees (managers, supervisors, hourly employees, part-time employees, etc.) are included in each pool of persons to be tested.

h. Unless otherwise specified, Tests will be conducted quarterly. Number of persons to be tested quarterly will be no more than 10.

i. Random Drug Testing will be for drugs listed in the policy only and not for alcohol.

j. USF will pay for the cost of the testing. The lab will retain samples in accordance with state or federal law, so that the employee may requests a retest of a the sample at his expense.

The testing for drugs will be administered by a means selected by the certified independent medical facility. At the time the specimens are tested, two samples shall be taken and a third if requested by the employee. Two samples will be sent to the laboratory to be tested at the employer’s expense. In order to be considered positive, the sample must show positive results on the Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (“GC/MS”) confirmatory test.

The third sample or specimen shall be collected in a separate container and shall be sealed in the presence of a medical facility witness with evidence tape, which tape shall be signed by the witness. Circumstances or conditions which may support such a belief include, but are not limited to: impairment or deterioration of job performance; exhibition of abnormal mental or physical conditions or behavior; observations relating to speech, appearance, and/or body odor; engaging in or exhibiting conduct which jeopardizes the safety of the workplace, employees, property, or other persons; regulatory or Company rule violations. 2 · Term
Article XXIV (“Term of Agreement”), Section 1 – This section shall be amended as follows:
Section 1. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect for the period from July 1, 2026, through and including June 30, 2027, and from year to year thereafter unless notice of termination or modification is given in writing by either party sixty (60) days prior to the anniversary date of June 30, 2027, such notice being sent by registered or certified mail. Both parties understand that in the event the Employer’s contract with the City of Philadelphia for Operations, Maintenance and Support Services at the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility is canceled or terminated for any reason, the Employer is not bound by this Agreement.

3 · Payroll
Article XXI (“Wages”), Section 2 – This section shall be amended as follows:
Section 2. All wages are to be paid weekly (accruals for UTO/STO shall remain bi-weekly).

chunks.title: 2026–27 Tentative Agreement
chunks.text:
4 · General Wage Increase (GWI)
Article XXI (“Wages”), Section 1 – This section shall be amended as follows:
Section 1. The wage rates and classifications that apply are shown in Exhibit “B.”
1. Effective July 1, 2026 – 1.5%
Exhibit “B” shall be modified to reflect the agreed upon wage increase.
The July 1, 2026, wage increase shall be retroactive to July 1, 2026. Retroactive payments will be made within thirty (30) days of ratification in the employee’s regular paycheck.

5 · Layoffs
Article V (“Seniority Rights”), Section 6 – A new Section 6 shall be added as follows:
Section 6. The Employer will not lay off bargaining unit members to help pay for July 1, 2026, wage increase set forth in Article XXI, Section 1. There is no expectation for any layoffs for the duration of this Agreement, but there is no guarantee there will not be any layoffs due to unforeseen or emergency circumstances.

6 · Pension
Article XX (“Pension”), Section 3 – This section shall be amended as follows:
Section 3. It is agreed that the Employer’s contribution to the Pension Fund shall be:
1. Effective July 1, 2026 – $2.65 per hour worked (capped at 40 hours)
It is agreed that all Employer contributions shall be made within thirty (30) days after the date required by the Trustees. Contributions will be made to the address supplied by the Pension Fund, as that may change from time to time.

chunks.title: 2026–27 Tentative Agreement
chunks.text:
7 · Badge Pulling
Article XXIII (“Miscellaneous”), Section 6 – This section shall be amended as follows:
Section 6. All discipline shall be imposed on an employee within ten (10) days from the date the Employer first became aware of the incident leading to the discipline, unless the Union agrees to an extension of time, or unless the discipline is the result of action by the City. Requests by the Employer for additional time will not be unreasonably rejected. The employer represents that it will not initiate contact with the Prison with the sole purpose of seeking to have an employee barred from the prison.
The Employer will adhere to the Prison’s current policy concerning “badge pulling” of employees. This includes, under certain circumstances, the Prison allowing the Employer to determine the level of discipline for certain violations. The imposition of this discipline shall be for just cause.
As set forth above, the Employer will have ten (10) days to impose discipline from the time the Prison concludes their investigation and informs the Employer of same.

chunks.title: 2026–27 Tentative Agreement
chunks.text:
8 · Forced Overtime (“Hooking”)
The parties agree to schedule an internal labor/management committee meeting to meet and confer regarding the Employer’s current use of “hooking,” or forced overtime. Nothing shall be binding unless mutually agreed to and set forth in writing by the parties during this meeting.
Article XVII (“Hours of Work”), Section 9 – A new Section 9 shall be added as follows:
Section 9. In the event that the Employer “hooks” an employee to work forced overtime, the Employer shall attempt to give at least one (1) hours’ notice to the employee, unless such notice is impracticable.
